questionText:
Sahiba wants to pursue animal husbandry as her field of study.

Describe how studying biology makes it easier for her to pursue her field of interest.
modelAnswer: Animal husbandry is the agricultural branch concerned with breeding, feeding, housing, and healthcare of domesticated animals. Studying biology provides the foundational knowledge of animal physiology, genetics, reproductive cycles, and nutrition required for successful breeding and livestock management, as well as an understanding of pathogens and immunology needed to prevent, diagnose, and treat livestock diseases.

questionText:
The given graph represents the effect of temperature on the activity of three different enzymes (P, Q, and R).

a. Interpret the curve for enzyme Q at 20°C. (1 Mark)
b. Identify the enzyme that works best at temperature above 25°C. (1 Mark)
c. Why does the curve for enzyme R show a fall after 45°C? (1 Mark)
modelAnswer:
a. At 20°C, enzyme Q reaches its peak reaction rate, showing that 20°C is its optimum temperature.
b. Enzyme R works best at temperatures above 25°C (its optimum is at ~40–45°C).
c. Above 45°C, high thermal kinetic energy disrupts hydrogen and ionic bonds stabilizing the tertiary structure of enzyme R, denaturing its active site so the substrate can no longer bind.

questionText: Mention any THREE drawbacks of the two-kingdom classification system.
modelAnswer:
1. It failed to distinguish between prokaryotes and eukaryotes, grouping bacteria and cyanobacteria under Kingdom Plantae.
2. It grouped photosynthetic autotrophs (green plants) and non-photosynthetic heterotrophs (fungi) in the same kingdom (Plantae), despite fungi lacking chlorophyll and having chitinous cell walls.
3. It could not appropriately place unicellular organisms with dual plant-like and animal-like characteristics (e.g. Euglena, which has chlorophyll and flagella).

questionText:
The given graph shows the effect of exercise on the breathing rates of persons X and Y. The breathing rate of both individuals is significantly increased.

a. With reference to the given graph, identify the unfit person with a valid reason. (2 Marks)
b. Why is the increased breathing rate important for both persons, X and Y? (1 Mark)
modelAnswer:
a. Person X is the unfit person (1 mark). Reason: Person X has a higher resting pulse/breathing rate before exercise, experiences a sharper pulse increase during exercise, and takes a significantly longer recovery time after exercise to return to the baseline resting level compared to Person Y (1 mark).
b. Increased breathing rate supplies additional oxygen required by working muscle cells for aerobic cellular respiration to generate ATP, and rapidly expels excess carbon dioxide and clears lactic acid debt produced during strenuous physical exertion (1 mark).

questionText:
The given diagram illustrates the activity of three enzymes in the duodenum of human beings.

Classify the enzymes, I, II and III, as intracellular or extracellular.

| Intracellular Enzyme | Extracellular Enzyme |
| :--- | :--- |
| | |
modelAnswer:
| Intracellular Enzyme | Extracellular Enzyme |
| :--- | :--- |
| Enzyme II | Enzyme I, Enzyme III |

Enzyme II acts within the microvilli/epithelial cells of the duodenum (intracellular brush-border enzyme). Enzymes I and III act in the lumen of the duodenum outside epithelial cells (extracellular secretions from pancreas and intestinal glands).

questionText:
EITHER

The given diagram shows some organelles of animal cell.

i. Identify the labelled organelles, X and Y. (2 Marks)
ii. Describe any ONE structural feature of each labelled organelle (X and Y). (2 Marks)
iii. Describe the arrangement of the organelles X and Y within the cell with reference to their proximity to the nucleus and their functional interrelationship. (2 Marks)
modelAnswer:
i. Organelle X: Rough Endoplasmic Reticulum (RER) (1 mark); Organelle Y: Golgi apparatus / Golgi body / Golgi complex (1 mark).
ii. Structural features:
- Organelle X (RER): A convoluted network of interconnected membranous tubules and flattened sacs (cisternae) studded with ribosomes on its outer cytosolic surface (1 mark).
- Organelle Y (Golgi apparatus): Stacks of flattened, membrane-bound, curved sacs (cisternae) with distinct forming (cis) and maturing (trans) faces, surrounded by budding transport vesicles (1 mark).
iii. Arrangement & functional interrelationship:
- Proximity: The RER (X) is located directly adjacent to and continuous with the outer nuclear membrane, while the Golgi apparatus (Y) lies nearby between the RER and the cell membrane (1 mark).
- Functional relationship: Proteins synthesized by ribosomes on the RER are packaged into transport vesicles that bud off and travel to the Golgi apparatus for chemical modification, sorting, and packaging into secretory vesicles (1 mark).
modelAnswerOrigin: E-marking checking hint & supplementary model answer

questionText:
OR

Compare aerobic and anaerobic respiration by mentioning any

i. THREE similarities. (3 Marks)
ii. THREE differences. (3 Marks)
modelAnswer:
i. THREE similarities (3 Marks):
1. Both pathways utilize glucose (or organic respiratory substrates) as the starting fuel source.
2. Both pathways initiate with the biochemical process of glycolysis in the cytoplasm.
3. Both pathways generate cellular energy in the form of adenosine triphosphate (ATP).
(Alternative accepted similarities: both involve pyruvate as an intermediate; both utilize enzymes and coenzymes like NAD).

ii. THREE differences (3 Marks):
1. Aerobic respiration requires molecular oxygen ($O_2$); anaerobic respiration occurs without oxygen.
2. Aerobic respiration takes place in both cytoplasm and mitochondria; anaerobic respiration occurs entirely within the cytoplasm.
3. Aerobic respiration yields high amounts of ATP (~36–38 ATP per glucose molecule); anaerobic respiration yields only 2 ATP per glucose molecule.
(Alternative accepted differences: End products of aerobic are $CO_2$ and $H_2O$; end products of anaerobic are lactic acid or ethanol and $CO_2$. Aerobic involves complete oxidation; anaerobic involves incomplete oxidation).

questionText:
EITHER

The ultrasound report of a patient’s stomach indicates the failure of closure of both the esophageal sphincter (cardiac sphincter) and pyloric sphincter.

i. Describe the effect of the given medical condition on the flow of food digestion. (2 Marks)
ii. Write ONE symptom each associated with the malfunctioning of both the sphincters. (2 Marks)
iii. Describe the process of peristalsis in moving the bolus through the esophagus. (2 Marks)
modelAnswer:
i. Effect on digestion flow (2 Marks): Failure of the esophageal (cardiac) sphincter causes acidic gastric chyme to reflux upward into the esophagus (acid reflux). Failure of the pyloric sphincter causes premature dumping of acidic, partially digested food into the duodenum before gastric chemical digestion is complete, and can also allow alkaline duodenal contents and bile to backflow into the stomach.
ii. Symptoms (2 Marks):
- Cardiac sphincter malfunction: Heartburn (burning sensation behind the sternum / acid indigestion / regurgitation).
- Pyloric sphincter malfunction: Nausea / vomiting of bile / severe abdominal pain / dumping syndrome / duodenal ulceration.
iii. Process of peristalsis (2 Marks): Peristalsis consists of involuntary, coordinated wave-like contractions of the muscular wall of the esophagus. Circular muscles contract behind the bolus to narrow the lumen and push the food downward, while longitudinal muscles ahead of the bolus contract to shorten and widen the tube, propelling the bolus into the stomach.

questionText:
OR

The given diagrams show the flow of blood in different chambers of the human heart.

Describe each diagram with reference to the state of chambers and the flow of blood. (6 Marks)
modelAnswer:
Diagram I: Atrial Systole / Ventricular Diastole (2 Marks)
- State of chambers: Atria are contracted; ventricles are relaxed.
- Blood flow: Contraction of atria forces oxygenated blood from left atrium through bicuspid (mitral) valve into left ventricle, and deoxygenated blood from right atrium through tricuspid valve into right ventricle. Aortic and pulmonary semilunar valves remain closed.

Diagram II: Ventricular Systole / Atrial Diastole (2 Marks)
- State of chambers: Ventricles are contracted; atria are relaxed.
- Blood flow: Increased ventricular pressure forces atrioventricular (bicuspid and tricuspid) valves shut to prevent backflow into atria (causing the first heart sound 'lub'), while aortic and pulmonary semilunar valves are forced open, ejecting blood into the aorta (systemic circulation) and pulmonary artery (pulmonary circulation).

Diagram III: Joint Diastole / Complete Cardiac Diastole (2 Marks)
- State of chambers: Both atria and ventricles are relaxed.
- Blood flow: Blood returns under low pressure from superior and inferior vena cavae into right atrium, and from pulmonary veins into left atrium. Blood flows passively through open atrioventricular valves into the ventricles. Semilunar valves snap closed to prevent arterial backflow (causing the second heart sound 'dup').
modelAnswerOrigin: E-marking checking hint & supplementary model answer
officialMarkingNotes:
Question No. 7b
Question Text: The given diagrams show the flow of blood in different chambers of the human heart. Describe each diagram with reference to the state of chambers and the flow of blood. (6 Marks)
SLO No.: 9.7.3
Max Marks: 6
Cognitive Level: U
Checking Hints (2 marks per diagram):
- Diagram I (Atrial systole / ventricular filling): 1 mark for state of chambers (atria contracted, ventricles relaxed); 1 mark for blood flow (blood pumped through open AV valves into ventricles; semilunar valves closed).
- Diagram II (Ventricular systole / ventricular emptying): 1 mark for state of chambers (ventricles contracted, atria relaxed); 1 mark for blood flow (AV valves closed, semilunar valves open, blood pumped into aorta and pulmonary artery).
- Diagram III (Joint diastole / general filling): 1 mark for state of chambers (both atria and ventricles relaxed); 1 mark for blood flow (blood fills atria and passively flows into ventricles; semilunar valves closed).
Overall Performance: Most candidates chose 7b. Better responses precisely named each cardiac phase, specified valve actions, and traced blood flow directions.
